cards.text: The apostle Paul, with Silvanus and Timothy, is writing to the church of the Thessalonians (1 Thessalonians 1:1), believers who have suffered at the hands of their own countrymen (1 Thessalonians 2:14). The writers have been torn away from them for a short time. In person, they say, but not in heart.

cards.question: While they're torn away from the Thessalonians, Paul and his companions say their desire to see them face to face is even more intense.

cards.text: Paul and his companions want to come back, and Paul himself tries AGAIN and AGAIN. Busy signal. Redial. Busy signal. REDIAL.

cards.question: Paul tried again and again to get back to the Thessalonians. Who does he say obstructed them?
Paul and his companions ask who their hope, their joy and their crown of boasting will be in the presence of the Lord Jesus at His coming. Who do they say it is?

cards.text: Then Paul writes that when they could bear it no longer, "we were willing to be left on our own in Athens." Friend, I got left in a junk drawer for years, and these guys at least get ATHENS.

So they send Timothy, their brother and fellow worker for God in the gospel of Christ. Before I sent out my invitations, my only fellow worker was this MUSTACHE, and friend, it argues with me on EVERY batch.

cards.question: Timothy is sent so the Thessalonians would be ___ and encouraged in their faith.

cards.text: That way none of them would be shaken by these trials. Paul writes, "For you know that we are destined for this."

cards.question: When Paul and his companions were with the Thessalonians, they promised them that faith would keep them from persecution.

cards.text: When Paul can't bear it any longer, he sends to find out about their faith, afraid the tempter had somehow tempted them. Friend, that's me yanking the oven door open every thirty seconds to check a batch, except Paul can't even PEEK.

cards.question: Paul fears the tempter had tempted the Thessalonians, and that the labor of Paul and his companions might have been in ___.

cards.text: Then, just now, Timothy is back from his visit. I bet Paul's holding his breath, like when the boss leans in and says, "Got a minute?"

cards.question: Timothy is back from his visit to the Thessalonians. What does he bring back?

answers.text: Good news about their faith and love
Good news about their growing numbers
Good news about the end of their trials

cards.question: Timothy reports that the Thessalonians long to see Paul and his companions, just as Paul and his companions long to see them.

cards.text: Paul and his companions are in distress and persecution, but this news about the Thessalonians' faith reassures them. That's the made-it-home-safe text landing in the middle of a ROUGH week.

cards.question: Paul and his companions say they can go on living, as long as the Thessalonians keep standing ___ in the Lord.

cards.text: In return for their great joy over the Thessalonians, Paul and his companions ask how they could ever thank God enough. Friend, I've been asking that same question every day since the angel called me out of that junk drawer, and I STILL don't have an answer.

cards.question: Paul and his companions pray night and day to see the Thessalonians face to face. What do they want to do when they get there?

answers.text: Supply what is lacking in their faith

cards.text: Then Paul writes, "Now may our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus, direct our way to you." He goes on: may the Lord make the Thessalonians' love increase and overflow, just as the writers' love for them overflows.

cards.question: Paul writes: may the Lord make the Thessalonians' love overflow, but only for fellow believers.
Paul wants the Lord to make the Thessalonians' love overflow. What purpose does he give for it?

answers.text: Blameless and holy hearts when Jesus comes
Peace with the people persecuting them

cards.text: Paul looks ahead to the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His saints, and he caps it off with an Amen. Friend, the first time I read that, I yelled AMEN so loud I flung a whole tray of cookies across the bakery, and I just LEFT them there.
